name: cubic_signature_tensor_todd_reduction
precondition: Toffoli-level IRCircuit (family dv_recon), measurement-free, gate names drawn only from {ccz, ccx, cx, x, z, s, sdg, t, tdg, h}, at least 4 ccz/ccx gates, and at least one Hadamard-free op range containing >= 2 ccz/ccx gates (api.dv.segments(ops, cut=('h',)) must return such a range). 4 <= qubits <= 20. No ancillas, no measurement, no continuous rotations. Circuits with Rz rotations (qft/qpe/hhl/qae/tfim) and circuits whose Toffolis are all isolated between Hadamards produce no match and cost nothing.
identity: TODD / Reed-Muller reduction of the CUBIC PHASE POLYNOMIAL, not of rotations. Take each Hadamard-free segment; it is a diagonal unitary U_f, f: F2^n -> Z8, since cx/x are linear and ccz/t are diagonal. Push the linear maps to the front with api.phasepoly.labels, so each ccz(p,q,r) contributes the degree-3 monomial l_p l_q l_r and each t/tdg contributes a degree-1 term, over the affine parity labels l. Represent f canonically by its SIGNATURE MATRIX S in F2^{n x m}: f(x) = sum_{l=1..m} (pi/4) * <s_l, x> with all coefficients odd, so the segment's T-count is exactly m (the number of columns). Expanding each ccz by 8*xyz = (x)+(y)+(z)-(x^y)-(y^z)-(x^z)+(x^y^z) gives the initial S with 7 columns per ccz, then equal columns are merged (two equal odd columns sum to a Clifford S gate). Then iterate the duplicate-and-destroy move: for every ordered pair of columns (a, b), set z = s_a AND s_b (entrywise product over F2) and update every column by s_l -> s_l XOR (<s_l-dependent parity> * z) in the way that leaves the symmetric third-order tensor T_{ijk} = sum_l s_{l,i} s_{l,j} s_{l,k} (and the lower-order data) invariant; after the update columns a and b coincide, and a duplicated pair is destroyed because T^2 = S is Clifford. Each successful move lowers m by 2 and emits one tracked Clifford correction (S/Z/CZ) that is appended to the segment's Clifford skeleton. Run moves greedily to a fixed point; then, as the second stage, do the Amy-Mosca refinement: the set of all signature matrices with the same tensor is a coset of the punctured Reed-Muller code RM(n-4, n)*, so search that coset locally (random walks of low-weight code additions, keeping the best) for a representative of smaller Hamming weight, i.e. fewer odd columns. Finally re-emit the segment as cx/t/tdg over the recovered parities (a CNOT network per column, synthesized by Gaussian elimination on the parity set) followed by the accumulated Clifford.
correctness: A Hadamard-free Clifford+T+CCZ circuit is a linear reversible map composed with a diagonal unitary U_f, and U_f is determined exactly by the Z8-valued polynomial f, hence by its coefficients of degree 1, 2 and 3 taken mod 8, mod 4 and mod 2 respectively. The degree-3 part mod 2 is precisely the symmetric tensor T_{ijk} built from the signature matrix; two signature matrices with the same T (and the same lower-order data after the recorded Clifford fix-ups) define the SAME diagonal unitary up to Clifford, which is why the duplicate-and-destroy update is an exact identity and not an approximation: it is verified column-algebraically over F2 before emission, and the emitted Clifford correction accounts for every term that changed modulus class. Destroying a duplicated pair uses T(p) T(p) = S(p), exact. The coset statement is the standard one: f's degree-<=3 representations differ exactly by elements of the punctured Reed-Muller code, so every coset element yields the same unitary; minimizing Hamming weight in the coset is minimizing T-count, and any candidate is re-checked by recomputing the tensor. Equivalence of the rewritten segment is further proved in O(ops) by api.phasepoly.witness (the Hadamard-free class is exactly where that witness is valid), and the judge then certifies the changed window exactly in D[omega], both sides being Clifford+T. Zero error is drawn: error_class exact, no ledger charge, no ancillas, no measurement, same qubit count.
trigger: One match per Hadamard-free segment returned by api.dv.segments(ops, cut=('h',)) that contains >= 2 ccz/ccx gates (gf2^4_mult has long ccz runs: the trigram 'ccz ccz ccz' occurs 4 times and only 14 Hadamards serve 16 ccz, so adjacent Toffolis sharing a target leave their conjugating Hadamards cancelled and the runs are long). Build S for the segment, run TODD to a fixed point and then the RM coset walk with a fixed seed and a fixed iteration cap (deterministic). Emit the match only if the final column count m_new is strictly less than the segment's current T-count and the re-emitted CNOT network does not raise the lexicographic cost; otherwise emit nothing for that segment. Segments with a single ccz cannot reduce (no pair of columns to duplicate) and are skipped, which is a trigger miss, not a rejection.
expected_effect: The 16 ccz gates currently cost 7 T each (112 T). Fusing the expanded signature columns inside each Hadamard-free run already collapses the shared parities between Toffolis that act on overlapping label sets, and the TODD moves then remove T gates in pairs; the RM coset walk picks up what TODD's greedy fixed point leaves. This is the mechanism that is documented to take GF(2^4)-mult from 112 T to 68 T (Tpar/TODD) and below it with Reed-Muller coset decoding. Because our segments are cut by the 14 Hadamards, the cross-segment merges that a global gadgetized treatment would get are not available, so I estimate landing near 64 T rather than the best published number: 112 -> ~64, i.e. 48 T removed, beating pyzx's 68. Conservative floor if the coset walk adds nothing beyond the greedy fixed point in the cut segments: ~76 T (36 saved). Qubits stay 12; CNOT count rises by roughly 30-60 from re-synthesizing the parity networks, which is only the third lexicographic key. Not a repeat of the floor: the floor merges first-order rotations as Pauli exponentials (degree-1 phase gadgets) and never touches the degree-3 part of the phase polynomial, which is where every T in this circuit lives.
source: L. E. Heyfron and E. T. Campbell, 'An efficient quantum compiler that reduces T count', Quantum Sci. Technol. 4, 015004 (2019) [TODD/TOOL, arXiv:1712.01557]; M. Amy, D. Maslov, M. Mosca, 'Polynomial-time T-depth optimization of Clifford+T circuits via matroid partitioning' (Tpar, 2014); M. Amy and M. Mosca, 'T-count optimization and Reed-Muller codes', IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 65 (2019) [arXiv:1601.07363].
